WASHINGTON — Rep. Nydia M. Velázquez (D-NY) and Rep. Hank Johnson (D-GA), co-chairs of the Congressional Hepatitis Caucus, reintroduced a resolution recognizing July 28, 2026 as World Hepatitis Day, raising awareness about the issues surrounding hepatitis B and C and reaffirming Congress's commitment to ending these preventable diseases.

Each year, thousands of Americans die of viral hepatitis, and another 75,000 are infected. Worldwide, an estimated 520 million people are chronically infected with hepatitis B and C, and an estimated 1.3 million die annually. Hepatitis B and hepatitis C, and the liver disease they cause, remain urgent global health threats, disproportionately impacting communities of color, LGBTQ individuals, and people who inject drugs.

“Far too many Americans have died because of hepatitis, a viral disease that disproportionately affects communities of color and the LGBTQ community,” said Congresswoman Velázquez. “I'm proud to reintroduce this resolution recognizing hepatitis as a public health priority. With increased public education, improved testing, and access to treatment, we can turn the tide on this epidemic. But this Administration has chosen to walk away from decades of proven vaccine policy, putting newborns at risk of a preventable disease. We cannot let that stand.”

“How we respond to preventable diseases says a great deal about our values,” said Rep. Johnson. “Every family deserves access to accurate information, lifesaving treatments, and quality healthcare. As we recognize World Hepatitis Day, we must continue investing in the public health tools that save lives and protect future generations.”

The reintroduction comes amid an unprecedented rollback of federal hepatitis prevention policy. After firing all 17 members of the CDC's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP), Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s reconstituted committee voted in December to end the longstanding recommendation that all newborns receive a hepatitis B vaccine dose at birth, a policy in place since 1991 that drove a dramatic reduction in pediatric hepatitis B infections. The CDC adopted the change over the objections of the American Academy of Pediatrics, the American Medical Association, and public health experts nationwide.

The Administration has also suspended U.S. support for global health institutions including USAID, the World Health Organization, and Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, jeopardizing hepatitis prevention programs abroad.

The resolution is endorsed by: African Health Coalition Incorporation, American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases, Association of Asian Pacific Community Health Organizations (AAPCHO), Coalition Against Hepatitis for People of African Origin (CHIPO), Community HealthCare Network, Community Liver Alliance, Congolese United Foundation, ekiM For Change, Empire Liver Foundation, End Hep C SF, Hawaiʻi Health & Harm Reduction Center, Health Betterment Initiative, Hep Free Hawaiʻi, Hep B United, Hepatitis B Foundation, Hepatitis C Allies of Philadelphia (HepCAP), HIV+Hepatitis Policy Institute, Housing Works - Positive Health Project, Illinois Public Health Association, Indiana Recovery Alliance, Liver Coalition of San Diego, Montefiore Starfish Program, NASTAD, National Harm Reduction Coalition, National Survivors Union, National Viral Hepatitis Roundtable (NVHR), North East Medical Services, SF HepB Free, The AIDS Institute, The Hepatitis C Mentor and Support Group, Inc. (HCMSG), Thomas Boyer Liver Research Institute, and VOCAL-NY.

“Amid federal public health funding declines and falling rates of the lifesaving hepatitis B vaccine, it is critical that we reaffirm our commitment to eliminating viral hepatitis,” said Chari Cohen, DrPH, MPH, President of the Hepatitis B Foundation. “We cannot allow the millions of people living with hepatitis B and hepatitis C in the U.S. and around the world to be left behind. Viral hepatitis elimination is possible, but requires sustained federal investment and strong congressional support to ensure that essential prevention, testing, care, and treatment services are accessible to all who need them.”

“We have taken a step back in our efforts to eliminate hepatitis over the past year and yet we have the tools to save lives. We must re-commit to the science-back strategies that we know prevents hepatitis B and C while increasing access to treatment,” said Heather Lusk, Co-Director of Hep Free Hawaiʻi and Executive Director of the Hawaiʻi Health & Harm Reduction Center.

“The Illinois Public Health Association (IPHA) is committed to recognizing World Hepatitis Day and the urgent need to expand testing, vaccination, accessible treatments, and global elimination of this deadly disease by 2030. Viral hepatitis claims more than 1.3 million lives annually and disproportionately impacts vulnerable populations across the globe and here in the United States. IPHA strongly supports World Hepatitis Day and our public health champions worldwide who work to increase vaccination, screening, and treatment for our impacted communities day in and day out!” said Jeffery Erdman, Deputy Executive Director of the Illinois Public Health Association.

A PDF of the resolution can be found here.

title: Velázquez and Johnson Reintroduce Resolution Recognizing World Hepatitis Day as Administration Rolls Back Vaccine Protections

ASHLAND, Ky. – Addiction Recovery Care, LLC (“ARC”), and its affiliates Pioneer Health Group, LLC and Science Hill Family Care, LLC, have agreed to a civil judgment of $16,205,774.05 in favor of the United States to resolve allegations that they defrauded the Kentucky Medicaid program. ARC, headquartered in Louisa, Kentucky, operates residential and outpatient drug rehabilitation facilities throughout the state. Along with its affiliates, ARC offers behavioral healthcare and medical healthcare services to patients at their rehabilitation facilities.

The judgment, announced today by the U.S. Attorney’s Office and the Office of the Kentucky Attorney General, is part of a civil settlement resolving allegations that ARC and its affiliates violated the False Claims Act, a federal statute that prohibits the submission of false claims for payment to Government programs, including the Medicaid program.

In April 2023, current and former employees of ARC filed a qui tam complaint alleging that ARC defrauded the Kentucky Medicaid program by submitting fraudulent claims for payment for behavioral health services provided in their drug rehabilitation programs. Under the qui tam provisions of the False Claims Act, a citizen can file a civil action on behalf of the United States to bring allegations of fraud to the Government’s attention. The United States thereafter opened a civil investigation into whether ARC violated the False Claims Act. During the Government’s investigation, ARC self-disclosed to the Government that it should not have billed for some of its services, including services identified by the whistleblowers in the qui tam complaint.

According to the settlement agreement, the Government alleged that ARC falsely represented the qualifications of some of their clinicians on claims to Kentucky Medicaid in order to receive higher reimbursements. From January 2018 to March 2024, some of ARC’s behavioral health services, such as psychotherapy, psychiatric evaluations, and mental health assessments, allegedly were provided by lower-level healthcare workers but billed as if ARC’s employees had higher-level licenses. Similarly, from July 2019 to mid-June 2021, the Government alleged that ARC falsely represented that it provided individual group therapy sessions, which Kentucky paid at a higher rate, when ARC in fact provided less expensive group therapy sessions. These alleged overstatements of provider qualifications and individualized care, which are commonly referred to as “upcoding,” are not allowed by federal health insurance programs and caused ARC and its affiliates to receive higher payments to which they were not entitled.

In addition to ARC’s purported upcoding practices, the Government alleged that, from January 2019 to December 2024, ARC’s affiliates billed duplicate office visits to Kentucky Medicaid and billed for office visits that were already reimbursed under an inclusive per diem rate. One of ARC’s affiliates also allegedly charged for care management services that did not meet Kentucky Medicaid’s coverage requirements, including services performed by ARC employees who lacked the necessary credentials.

The civil judgment and settlement agreement resolve the qui tam case captioned United States ex rel. Rikki Pope, et al. v. Addiction Recovery Care, LLC, Case No. 0:23-cv-51-DLB, which was recently unsealed by the Court. The amount of the judgment, which will be paid over several years, was negotiated and reduced due to Defendants’ financial condition and prospects for ongoing operations. As part of this resolution, the individuals who filed the qui tam complaint are eligible to receive a portion of the settlement proceeds.

This matter was investigated by the Affirmative Civil Enforcement section of the U.S. Attorney’s Office, with assistance from the U.S. Department for Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General, the Kentucky Office of Attorney General, Office of Medicaid Fraud and Abuse Control, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Meghan Stubblebine and former Assistant U.S. Attorney Katie Sheridan represented the United States.

The claims resolved by the settlement are allegations only; there has been no determination of liability.

– END –
title: Addiction Recovery Care and Affiliates Agree to Pay $16.2 Million Civil Judgment to Resolve Medicaid Fraud Allegations

Most Wanted COVID-19 Fraud Fugitive Returned from Jamaica to Face Charges in $32 Million Scheme
A fugitive on the FBI’s Most Wanted Fraudsters List was returned Saturday to the Southern District of Florida to face federal charges for her alleged role in a scheme that fraudulently obtained more than $32 million in federal COVID-19 relief funds.
Elaine Escoe, 41, was charged by indictment in 2025 with conspiracy to commit wire fraud, conspiracy to commit money laundering, and multiple substantive counts of wire fraud and money laundering. After a federal arrest warrant was issued in May 2025, Escoe failed to appear for her court appearance and fled to Jamaica. Acting on information developed by the FBI, Jamaican authorities captured Escoe after receiving a tip. She was returned to South Florida Saturday through the coordinated efforts of the FBI, the U.S. Marshals Service, the U.S. Department of State’s Diplomatic Security Service Regional Security Office at the U.S. Embassy in Kingston, the Jamaican Constabulary Force (JCF), and the JCF Jamaica Fugitive Apprehension Team.
“This Most Wanted Fraudster allegedly obtained tens of millions in COVID-19 relief, stealing critical resources from legitimate businesses during a national crisis,” said Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche. “She fled the country believing she could escape justice but ultimately could not. Those who exploit taxpayer-funded programs will be held accountable by this Department of Justice, no matter how long it takes or where they attempt to hide.”
“Elaine Angene Escoe’s arrest and return to the United States demonstrates that no one is beyond the reach of American justice,” said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the National Fraud Enforcement Division. “This Most Wanted Fraudster faces charges stemming from a multimillion-dollar scheme to defraud taxpayer-funded COVID-19 relief programs. The Fraud Division will continue to vigorously prosecute those who steal from the American people.”
“The historic success of the ‘Most Wanted Fraudster’ list continues as the FBI and our partners just captured our fourth Most Wanted Fraudster in 5 weeks, and yet another high value target returned to the U.S. by this FBI,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “Elaine Angene Escoe, on the run since May of 2025, was captured in Jamaica while living under a fake identity of ‘Harley Newman’ – and returned to the United States today to face justice. She is charged for her alleged involvement in a conspiracy to commit wire fraud and money laundering – connected with a scheme to fraudulently obtain over $32 million in federal COVID-19 relief funds. Escoe brings the number of high value targets returned by the FBI to over 30 just since June. Led by President Trump, Vice President Vance, and the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud – the FBI and our partners continue to see an unprecedented level of success taking down the worst of the worst alleged fraudsters. In just week weeks, we have captured four subjects on three different continents charged with a combined nearly $1.8 billion in fraud, collectively on the run for over 3,500 days, each hiding overseas – now returned and all in custody in 1.5 months. Under this administration, fraud is no longer tolerated – and those who steal from American taxpayers have nowhere to hide.”
“Elaine Escoe allegedly helped orchestrate a sprawling scheme that fraudulently obtained more than $32 million from programs created to keep American businesses and workers afloat during the pandemic,” said U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida. “After being charged, she failed to appear in court and fled to Jamaica. Defendants cannot escape accountability simply by leaving the country. Thanks to the determined work of our federal, state, and international partners, she is back in South Florida and will now face the charges against her. This coordinated effort demonstrates that we will pursue fugitives wherever they go and bring them back to face justice.”
According to court records, Escoe and her co-conspirators submitted or caused the submission of fraudulent applications seeking more than $32 million in Paycheck Protection Program (PPP), Restaurant Revitalization Fund (RRF), Shuttered Venue Operators Grant (SVOG), and Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) funds. The applications falsely represented the existence, payroll, revenue, and operations of purported businesses to qualify for and maximize federal relief funding.
To support the fraudulent applications, the conspirators created fake tax documents, fabricated bank records, and other false financial records that lenders and program administrators relied upon in approving loans and grants. Some applications were submitted on behalf of businesses controlled by the conspirators, while others were submitted for third parties in exchange for substantial kickbacks — sometimes as much as 50% of the loan proceeds. The fraud proceeds were subsequently laundered among the conspirators.
Escoe is the last remaining defendant charged in the scheme. Following a December 2025 trial, Alfred Davis, Cher Davis, and Latoya Clark were convicted by a federal jury. James McGhow and Gino Jourdan previously pleaded guilty. Alfred Davis was sentenced to 235 months in prison, Cher Davis to 87 months, Clark to 70 months, Jourdan to 46 months, and McGhow to 42 months.
FBI Miami’s West Palm Beach Resident Agency is investigating the case, with assistance from Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Miami and the Palm Beach County State Attorney’s Office.
On June 4, the FBI announced the creation of the Most Wanted Fraudsters List. The list included Herb Kimble, a fugitive in a $1.2 billion telemedicine and durable medical equipment scheme, who, on June 8 — just four days later — was apprehended in the Philippines and was soon after charged as part of the 2026 National Health Care Fraud Takedown. On June 8, Escoe was added to the Most Wanted Fraudsters List, and she was apprehended less than two months later.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Southern District of Florida at www.flsd.uscourts.gov or at http://pacer.flsd.uscourts.gov, under case number 25-cr-80076.
title: Most Wanted COVID-19 Fraud Fugitive Returned from Jamaica to Face Charges in $32 Million Scheme

USNS Hector A. Cafferata Jr. Completes Acceptance Trials
27 July 2026
SAN DIEGO - USNS Hector A. Cafferata Jr. (ESB 8) successfully completed Acceptance Trials July 17 following a three-day underway off the coast of southern California. ESB 8 is the final Expeditionary Sea Base in production and is scheduled for delivery later this summer.
During the underway period, the ship conducted comprehensive tests to demonstrate performance of the ship’s major systems and its ability to operate safely and effectively.
“Our ESBs are at the forefront of maritime operations, bringing operational capability and rapid response capabilities to the fleet,” said Jon Thomas, Acting Program Manager, Strategic and Theater Sealift. “As the final ship of the class, ESB 8 demonstrated its full range of capabilities, and its readiness for delivery and fleet operations.”
ESBs are mobile sea-based assets and are a part of the critical access infrastructure that supports the deployment of forces, equipment, supplies, and warfighting capabilities. ESBs are highly flexible platforms designed to support a variety of maritime based missions.
Acceptance Trials of ESB 8 underscore the Navy’s commitment to building America’s Fleet of the Future. This trial marks the near conclusion of the new construction portion of the program. The first ESB of the class was delivered in 2015 and the ship has now been supporting the fleet for over a decade.
For 250 years, American naval power has projected strength globally, operating forward 24/7, 365 days a year. This operational tempo demands continuous capability, and the Fleet of the Future is our answer.
The Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) for Maritime is the single accountable organization for delivering surface ships for the U.S. Navy. This new centralized organizational construct will empower leaders with broader scope and greater authority to accelerate delivery of combat capability and ensure acquisition speed and discipline are driven by what the warfighter needs-when they need it.

text:
With this rule, USCIS can refer asylum applications to Immigration Judges without interviewing the alien
WASHINGTON – The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) released the following statement after U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) announced a rule change designed to reduce the backlog in the asylum system.
Currently, both USCIS and Department of Justice (DOJ) Immigration Judges adjudicate applications for asylum: USCIS adjudicates “affirmative” asylum applications for aliens who are not in removal proceedings, while Immigration Judges adjudicate “defensive” asylum applications for aliens who are in removal proceedings. Depending on the alien’s immigration status, USCIS will usually either adjudicate the application or refer it to an Immigration Judge, who will then conduct a new review of the application. This essentially allows an alien to get a second chance at asylum.
The interim final rule allows USCIS to refer asylum applications to Immigration Judges without first interviewing the alien. This rule will shorten the total time that it takes asylum officers and Immigration Judges to adjudicate asylum applications. Among other reasons, USCIS is making this change to reduce the asylum backlog.
“For far too long the asylum system has been exploited for purposes of delay and work authorization, not legitimate claims of protection,” said USCIS Director Joseph Edlow. “America’s asylum system exists to protect individuals who genuinely fear persecution and this rule will help ensure that resources are directed to the timely adjudication of those claims instead of to those seeking to use the system as a loophole.”
“One of the greatest barriers to effective immigration enforcement is intentional delay by illegal aliens and the open borders attorneys who represent them,” said DHS General Counsel James Percival. “My office works every day with the immigration components of DHS to improve efficiency and fulfill the President’s mandate. The rule would do just that.”
The new rule will go into effect immediately. USCIS will accept public comments and later issue a final rule responding to those comments.
# # #
title: USCIS Announces Rule Change to Asylum System to Reduce Backlog

HOUSTON - A 30-year-old Houston resident has pleaded guilty to concealing material support to a foreign terrorist organization and making false statements.

Anas Said is a pledged supporter of Islamic State of Iraq and al-Sham (ISIS) and used various social media accounts to post, share, or disseminate ISIS propaganda.

He also discussed ISIS propaganda using Telegram, where he received feedback on media he personally created. In one message, he discussed sending his clip to the Sarh al-Khilafah Institution, which agreed to publish it on their channel. According to court records, Sarh al-Khilafah, a/k/a Tower of the Caliphate, is a media entity that uses social media platforms to produce content ranging from operational security tips to guides on chemicals and explosives. They are also known for aggregating (ISIS) content online.

Said admitted to knowing Sarh al-Khilafah was a media entity working on behalf of, and in coordination with, ISIS. Prior to publishing his media, Said removed his name as designer of the video, thus concealing his material support of ISIS.

Said also pleaded guilty to lying to law enforcement regarding a weapon he possessed and discussed on social media. As part of the plea, he admitted to making the following statement: “I am thinking and hoping to kill the infidels with a weapon and as many people as possible in order to heal my heart.”

U.S. District Judge David Hittner accepted the plea on July 24 and will impose sentencing Oct. 16. At that time, Said faces up to 10 years in federal prison for concealing material support to a foreign terrorist organization and a maximum of five years for making material false statements. He could also be ordered to pay up to a $250,000 maximum fine on each count.

Said has been and will remain in custody pending sentencing.

FBI Houston’s Joint Terrorism Task Force (JTTF) conducted the investigation with special assistance from police departments in Houston and Sugar Land, as well as the Harris County Sheriff’s Office. The JTTF also includes Montgomery County Sheriff’s Office, Immigration and Customs Enforcement Homeland Security Investigations, Department of State’s Diplomatic Security Service, IRS Criminal Investigation, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, Secret Service, Houston Metro Police Department, Customs and Border Protection, and Federal Air Marshals Service. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Steven Schammel and Liesel Roscher prosecuted the case.
title: ISIS supporter admits to disseminating terrorist propaganda via social media

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Following disturbing reports that the Department of Defense removed the names of four American troops from the official Iran War death toll, Rep. Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06) joined 14 fellow Democratic veterans in urging the Administration to accurately and transparently account for U.S. servicemembers killed and wounded in the Iran war.

“As veterans of America’s wars, we have serious concerns about reports that the Department of War is delaying, removing or otherwise mischaracterizing the release of information about wounded and killed U.S. servicemembers,” wrote the lawmakers.

“The U.S. government owes U.S. servicemembers, their families, and every American the truth about all U.S. casualties in the War with Iran. It is imperative that these reports are timely, accurate and adequately explain the reason for amended or delayed reports,” they continued. “We urge you to commit to releasing timely and accurate information on all injuries and deaths of U.S. servicemembers.”

Following public outcry, the Department of Defense quietly restored the names of the four U.S. servicemembers removed from the Iran War death toll over the weekend. The Administration has not provided an adequate explanation as to why the servicemembers were removed in the first place.

The letter, led by Rep. Mike Thompson (CA-04), was also signed by Representatives Pat Ryan (NY-18), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Chris Deluzio (PA-17), Derek Tran (CA-45), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Maggie Goodlander (NH-02), Eugene Vindman (VA-07), Jason Crow (CO-06), Bobby Scott (VA-03), Salud Carbajal (CA-24), Gil Cisneros (CA-31), and Jared Golden (ME-02).

The full text of the letter can be found here and below.

Dear President Trump,

As veterans of America’s wars, we have serious concerns about reports that the Department of War is delaying, removing or otherwise mischaracterizing the release of information about wounded and killed U.S. servicemembers.

The U.S. government owes U.S. servicemembers, their families, and every American the truth about all U.S. casualties in the War with Iran. It is imperative that these reports are timely, accurate and adequately explain the reason for amended or delayed reports. Inaccurate and delayed reports from the Department of War about U.S. casualties is bad for morale and undermines our U.S. servicemembers.

We urge you to commit to releasing timely and accurate information on all injuries and deaths of U.S. servicemembers.

Sincerely,
title: Democratic Veterans Demand Transparency on Iran War Casualties

In alignment with the Department of War-driven transition to the ‘Warfighting Acquisition System,’ the Air Force has designated Portfolio Acquisition Executives for all 17 of its acquisition portfolios. The transition from Program Executive Officers to PAEs, decentralizes authorities and resources by mission to ensure accountability and accelerate the delivery of urgently needed capabilities to warfighters.
“As we transition to a Warfighting Acquisition System, it felt absolutely essential for us to accelerate getting these authorities out to the field,” said Secretary of the Air Force for Acquisition, Technology and Logistics William Bailey.
“Our initial group of PAEs allowed us to examine what a PAE could do and what barriers in our organization needed to be knocked down. Aligning authority and accountability at the point of execution is essential to winning the fight.”
In January, the service transitioned the first five PEOs to PAEs — Command, Control, Communications and Battle Management; Fighters and Advanced Aircraft; Nuclear Command, Control and Communications; Propulsion; and Weapons. That initial tranche of PAEs served as pathfinders, guiding what transformation would look like for other portfolios, which followed suit by applying lessons learned. As of July 4, the Air Force PAEs are:
While this redesignation is a key milestone in transforming the DAF’s process, Bailey emphasized the acquisition community will continue to refine how it delivers capabilities.
“This is a monumental step forward but our work is not done. Pushing these critical decisions down to the PAE level demands a heightened commitment to delivering results and holding ourselves accountable. We [the acquisition community] must continue to be bold, to learn, and to adapt, ensuring we provide our warfighters with the decisive edge they need when they need it.”
This redesignation is one example of the DAF’s commitment to placing acquisition on a wartime footing, putting the warfighter at the center of its processes to ensure the voice of the operator informs the capabilities acquirers deliver.
title: Air Force delivers on acquisition transformation, redesignates executives as PAEs

text:
Concluding an eight-month science mission aboard the International Space Station, NASA astronaut Chris Williams returned to Earth on Sunday alongside Roscosmos cosmonauts Sergey Kud-Sverchkov and Sergei Mikaev.

The crew made its safe, parachute-assisted landing at 5:27 a.m. CDT (3:27 p.m., Kazakhstan time), southeast of Dzhezkazgan, after departing the space station at 2:03 a.m., aboard the Soyuz MS-28 spacecraft.

The crew was in space for 241 days, orbiting the Earth 3,856 times and traveling more than 102 million miles. They launched to the International Space Station on Nov. 27, 2025. The mission was the first for Williams and Mikaev and the second for Kud-Sverchkov.

While aboard the orbiting laboratory, Williams supported a wide range of scientific investigations and technology demonstrations. He helped advance research for new cancer treatments and improved in-space manufacturing of materials used in high-performance computers and electronics. Williams also completed two spacewalks to prep for space station power system upgrades and to replace a faulty joint on the Canadarm2 robotic arm. The crew’s work aboard the space station helps improve life on Earth and prepare for future human missions to the Moon and Mars.

Following post-landing medical checks, the crew members will fly by helicopter to Karaganda, Kazakhstan, where recovery teams are based. Williams then will board a NASA aircraft bound for the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston.

For more than 25 years, people have lived and worked continuously aboard the International Space Station, advancing scientific knowledge and making research breakthroughs not possible on Earth. The space station helps NASA understand and overcome the challenges of human spaceflight, expand commercial opportunities in low Earth orbit, and build on the foundation for long-duration missions to the Moon, as part of the Artemis program, and to Mars.

To learn more about International Space Station research, operations, and its crews, visit:

www.nasa.gov/station

For immediate release
Cory Thomas
United States Marshals Service
Western Arkansas Fugitive Task Force
(479) 650-2761
Houston, TX – After almost three weeks on run from justice, the U.S. Marshals tracked down and arrested Jasmine Johnston on Sunday, July 26, 2026. Johnston was wanted by the Fort Smith Police Department for Murder in the First Degree (class Y) and Aggravated Robbery – Armed (class Y).
The warrants stemmed from an incident that occurred in Fort Smith, Arkansas on July 7, 2026, close to State Police Headquarters. The investigation led the Fort Smith Police Department to charge Johnston with the offenses and to begin looking for her. The Fort Smith Police Department has a strong, long-standing relationship with the U. S. Marshals Service and both state and federal agencies began working together to locate Johnston. On Sunday, July 26, Johnston was located by the U.S. Marshals (Gulf Coast Task Force) in Houston, Texas at Huckberry Park. She was taken into custody without incident. “This is what happens when federal, state, and local agencies work together to keep our communities safe,” says Chief Deputy U.S. Marshal Cory Thomas.
U.S. Marshals Service task forces combine the efforts of federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies to locate and arrest the most dangerous fugitives. These task forces are dedicated to reducing violent crime by locating and apprehending wanted criminals. They also serve as the central point for agencies to share information on fugitive matters. In 2024, the U. S. Marshals arrested 74,222 fugitives, cleared 88,765 warrants, which averaged out to around 297 fugitives arrested per day in 2024 alone.

Secretary Wright issued an emergency order to stabilize the grid to mitigate the risk of blackouts across during hot weather conditions
July 26, 2026
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) issued an emergency order to keep Americans across 17 states powered during the region’s energy emergency brought on by hot weather conditions. The order directs the Southwest Power Pool, Inc. (SPP) to dispatch specified generation units and to order their operation as needed to maintain reliability. The order also authorizes SPP to direct backup generation resources to operate as a last resort before declaring an Energy Emergency Alert (EEA) 3 or during an EEA 3. The order was issued pursuant to a request from SPP.
“The Trump Administration is tapping into an abundant supply of unused backup generation to maintain affordable, reliable, and secure power for hardworking American families and businesses,” said U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright. “The previous administration’s energy subtraction policies weakened the grid, leaving Americans more vulnerable during emergency events. Thanks to President Trump’s leadership, we are reversing those failures and using every available tool to ensure Americans have continued access to affordable, reliable, and secure energy to power and cool their homes.”
DOE estimates more than 35 gigawatts (GW) of unused backup generation remain available nationwide.
On day one of his second term, President Trump declared a national energy emergency after the Biden administration’s energy subtraction agenda left behind a grid increasingly vulnerable to blackouts.
Power outages cost the American people $44 billion per year, according to data from DOE’s National Laboratories. This order mitigates the possibility of power outages in the region and highlights the commonsense policies of the Trump Administration to ensure Americans have access to affordable, reliable, and secure electricity.
The order is effective on July 26, 2026, and shall expire at 11:59 PM CDT on August 3, 2026.
###
title: Energy Secretary Secures Grid Across 17 States Amid Period of Hot Weather

Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries appeared on CNN’s State of the Union, where he outlined how with 100 days until the midterm elections, Democrats are going to continue to push back on Republican extremism and fight to lower costs for hardworking American taxpayers.

DANA BASH: Here with me now is the House Democratic Leader, Congressman Hakeem Jeffries. Mr. Leader, thank you so much for being here. I know that you are launching what Democrats are calling 100 Days Out Weekend of Action with more than 400 grassroots events in competitive states, including Pennsylvania, where you’re going to be speaking later today. At the same time, your party is fighting over whether the path back to the majority runs through the center or the activist left, who want to defund the police, abolish ICE, end aid to Israel, open borders. I know that you call the Democratic Party a mosaic, but are you going to push any of those positions if you win the majority back?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well what unites the party, and certainly what will take place over the next 100 days, beginning today, is a focus on us fighting for an affordable America, based on the reality that life in this country is far too expensive and everybody agrees that that’s the dynamic that the country confronts. Too many people are working hard, they’re playing by the rules, but they can’t thrive and they can barely survive. Not enough food on the table, not enough gas in the tank, unable to actually regularly and consistently afford to pay the rent or pay the mortgage. We want to drive down the cost of groceries, drive down and lower the cost of gasoline, drive down the cost of housing and also make sure that healthcare is affordable for every single American.

DANA BASH: Right, but to do those things, which is the messaging that I’ve heard you say, especially recently, you need to come up with policy proposals. So will those policy proposals be in line with what some of the more progressive members who keep getting elected are pushing? Or will you sort of move more towards the moderate area, where if you do win the majority, it will be likely because they pick up swing districts?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we want to make sure that we are solving problems on behalf of the American people, and that’s in every possible area. It is clear that what unites Democrats, for instance, we forcefully have been pushing back against the One Big Ugly Bill and the effort to enact the largest cut to Medicaid in American history. That’s a disgrace, and clearly that needs to be reversed. We need to make sure that we do things like extending the Affordable Care Act tax credits so that more than 20 million people actually can have healthcare that they can afford restored to them as opposed to the situation that they confront right now because of MAGA extremist policies, which is that they’ve experienced dramatic increases in their health insurance premiums in some cases more than $1000 per month. It certainly is the case, as we’ve already demonstrated unanimously on the House Floor, that we need to stop this reckless and costly war of choice that has skyrocketed gas prices on everyday Americans, and we need to stop the Trump tariffs, which have increased costs on everyday Americans by thousands of dollars per year.

DANA BASH: You, according to my colleague Manu Raju, clash with Senator Bernie Sanders over the fact that he is campaigning for progressive candidates, some of whom are challenging incumbents you back, including Members of the Congressional Black Caucus. Are Senator Sanders and other progressives in the party making it harder for you to win in November? Is that what you said to Senator Sanders?

LEADER JEFFRIES: No, I wouldn’t describe it as a clash. It was a candid conversation along with Congressman Greg Meeks, the Chair of the Congressional Black Caucus PAC, with respect to one particular race in North Carolina at the beginning of the primary cycle and trying to get a sense of his approach to that race. I do think that Senator Sanders and Democrats in both the House and the Senate understand the stakes that are in front of us, particularly as we are one hundred days out. And that’s making sure that we actually take back control of the Congress so we can end this MAGA extremism that has been unleashed on the American people that is actively hurting hardworking American taxpayers and actually commit to making life more affordable for the American people. That’s clearly what the American people want to see done, and that’s not what Republicans have been able to accomplish during their time in office since Trump was sworn in back in January of last year.

DANA BASH: I think one of the things that some of those who are winning their primaries and will likely be in office want to know is if you are going to agree to hold votes on abolishing ICE, opening borders, things of that nature. Will you?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, I’ve spoken to several of the incoming Members of Congress across the ideological spectrum. Not a single person has raised those issues, other than obviously what they’ve seen from Democrats in pushing back against an out-of-control ICE because we believe that immigration enforcement in this country clearly should be fair, just and humane, and that’s not what’s taking place. That’s the reason why House Democrats have taken a strong position as it relates to not giving a dime to Donald Trump’s violent mass deportation machine until, of course, there is dramatic reform in this country and that ICE agents actually start to conduct themselves like every other cop, police officer and law enforcement agent in the country.

DANA BASH: Your next-door neighbor, New Jersey, just disclosed that 6,600 non-citizens were mistakenly registered to vote there from 2023 to 2024. 400 of them actually voted in elections since then. It is a small number compared to the 7 million voters in New Jersey and there’s no evidence that that swayed any election. But this is one of the most significant disclosures of non-citizen registration. Democrats have repeatedly said that non-citizen voting doesn’t happen. It happened. Is this a problem?

LEADER JEFFRIES: I think that I continue to have confidence in state and local authorities in making sure that there’s going to be a free and fair election in November. And if modest or minor challenges emerge, such as the one that was disclosed voluntarily by the authorities in New Jersey, that it is immediately corrected. And that’s what I expect will continue to happen. Unfortunately, what we’ve seen from Donald Trump is that, in this particular case, Republicans have adopted voter suppression as an electoral strategy because they have failed to actually deliver on making life more affordable for the American people. It was Donald Trump who promised to lower costs on day one, but we know that costs haven’t gone down in this country, costs have gone up. It was Donald Trump, I believe, who said that he was elected not to start wars—endless wars in the Middle East—but to stop them, and then turned around and has gotten us involved in this reckless war of choice in Iran that has skyrocketed gas prices on the American people. By the way, it was Donald Trump who said they were going to love and cherish Medicaid, and then Republicans enacted the largest cut to Medicaid in American history, ripping healthcare away from more than 14 million Americans. They have nothing to run on. We’re going to run on fighting for an affordable America.

DANA BASH: Mr. Leader, before I let you go, President Trump ordered signs placed outside the Museum of American History, warning that it promotes inaccurate history. It comes, of course, as the White House is attacking the Smithsonian, accusing the institution of promoting left-wing ideology. Is there anything you can do to stop those signs from going up?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we’re going to explore every legislative avenue and every litigation avenue, as we’ve repeatedly done up until this point. Here’s the thing. Black history is American history, and we are not going to let the extremists whitewash it. Not now. Not ever.

DANA BASH: Hakeem Jeffries, Democratic Leader of the House of Representatives. Thanks so much for being here. I appreciate it.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Thank you.

Full interview can be watched here.

###
title: LEADER JEFFRIES ON CNN: “WE ARE FIGHTING FOR AN AFFORDABLE AMERICA”

text:
U.S. Marshals Conduct Operation Adam’s Watch to Recognize 20th Anniversary of Adam Walsh Act
For immediate release
Office of Public Affairs
Usms.mediadesk@usdoj.gov
WASHINGTON – The United States Marshals Service (USMS), along with state and local agencies in thirty-seven federal judicial districts and geographical locations across the United States, led a multi-week enforcement operation that resulted in the arrest of more than 330 fugitives wanted for failure to register as a sex offender, sex assault, or other sex offenses.
The arrests include 234 fugitives wanted on state charges for failure to register as a sex offender, including 5 offenders charged with violation of federal statute 18 USC 2250, failure to register as a sex offender. In addition, 96 fugitive sex offenders wanted on sex assault and other sex charges were located and arrested.
Operation Adam’s Watch, named in honor of Adam Walsh, was conducted to commemorate the 20th Anniversary of the signing of the Adam Walsh Act (AWA). The operation focused on identifying, locating, and apprehending non-compliant sex offenders, assisting our state and local partners with verifying offenders’ compliance with their mandated registration requirements.
"The USMS, having a robust network of federal, state, and local partners, was the logical choice to implement the Adam Walsh Act,” said U.S. Marshals Service Director Gadyaces Serralta. "We are the best in the world at finding people. We have the tools and the talent no one else has. When the Adam Walsh Act became law, it made sense for us, along with our partners, to make sure noncompliant sex offenders are back off the streets and not a threat to those who could become victims."
"As we observe Adam Walsh Remembrance Day and the 20th anniversary of the Adam Walsh Act, I'm reminded that my brother's legacy isn't defined by what happened to him, but by the lives that continue to be protected because people refused to let his story end in tragedy,” said Callahan Walsh, Executive Director of the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children. “Every time the U.S. Marshals Service apprehends an offender who threatens children, every time NCMEC helps law enforcement recover a missing child or support an investigation, we're carrying that legacy forward. Together, we're proving that the strongest tool we have to protect children is partnership."
Operation Adam’s Watch is representative of the ongoing efforts of the Marshals Service and its partners to keep communities safe by locating and apprehending fugitive sex offenders. Conducted over a multi-week period concluding on July 24, 2026, thirty-seven Federal judicial districts throughout the states of Alabama, Arizona, California, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Mississippi, Missouri, Nevada, New Hampshire, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Texas, and Virginia joined in the unified efforts to ensure the success of Operation Adam’s Watch.
Adam Walsh's abduction and murder served as a catalyst for change in the way the nation deals with crimes against children. This tragedy launched his parents, John and Reve Walsh, on a lifelong mission to prevent similar attacks on other children. The Walsh's efforts resulted in the establishment of the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children.
Annually, USMS conducts more than 200 sex offender operations, assisting state and local agencies with sex offender compliance and enforcement actions across the nation. Since inception of the Adam Walsh Act, the United States Marshals Service has opened 52,000 investigations for federal Failure to Register violations and closed by arrest more than 7,500 federal warrants for violations of 18 USC 2250). In addition to enforcement of the Adam Walsh Act, the United States Marshals Service prioritizes sex offense warrants under its fugitive mission. Since 2006, the Marshals Service and its fugitive task forces partners have closed by arrest 250,000 felony warrants for fugitives wanted on sex offense, sex assault, or failure to register related warrants.
The USMS has executed more than 5,300 sex offender compliance and enforcement operations, partnering with law enforcement officers from state and local law enforcement agencies in all 50 states and U.S. territories. During these operations, the U.S. Marshals Service assisted state and local enforcement partners with more than 842,000 compliance checks on known sex offenders.

Chief Master Sgt. of the Air Force David Wolfe and his wife, Dr. Wolfe, visited Malmstrom Air Force Base July 22-23, to meet with the Airmen and families responsible for upholding the nation's nuclear surety.
The two-day visit provided a firsthand look at 341st Missile Wing operations, giving Wolfe insight into the capabilities, challenges and support systems required to sustain the nuclear enterprise.
Wolfe met with operations, maintenance and security forces Airmen to discuss mission readiness and the demands of maintaining the Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missile force. The engagements highlighted the teamwork, precision and leadership required to keep the nation's most responsive leg of the nuclear triad on alert around the clock.
He also addressed Malmstrom AFB Airmen during an all-call to encourage candid discussion on leadership, quality of life, professional development and the future of the Air Force.
"If you're in a leadership position, that's the go-do from the boss and I: be really good at it and take care of our people the way they deserve to be taken care of," Wolfe said. "Listen to them, take their problems on and be the champion of their solutions."
Reflecting on his own career, Wolfe encouraged Airmen to embrace the high standards and sense of purpose that define Air Force Global Strike Command.
"The spirit and discipline that comes with being in Global Strike Command is what absolutely changed my young career ...," Wolfe said. "This is the place where you learn what the rules are, why it's important to follow those rules and the seriousness of what we do. Consider yourself lucky that you have the opportunity to serve in a place where the standard is the standard and that’s it."
Recognizing that mission readiness extends beyond operational capabilities, Dr. Doniel Wolfe focused on the families who enable the mission. She met with military spouses, key support liaisons and installation support organizations to discuss family readiness, resource accessibility and the unique challenges faced by families supporting the missile mission.
The visit reinforced the connection between Airmen, families and mission success, highlighting that the strength of Air Force Global Strike Command's nuclear deterrence mission depends on the resilience, readiness and support of its people.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Now, Democrats chose to hold Graham Platner accountable, and they have switched their candidates in Maine in the middle of a must-win race for the party. But take a listen to your House colleague, Speaker Mike Johnson, when asked about how he intends to handle allegations against two Members of his party on Tuesday.

RECORDING OF SPEAKER JOHNSON: The key word there is allegation. We have a process here—the House Ethics Committee works on those things. If allegations are made, they work through a process. So I’m not in the business of commenting on investigations as they are in process. And we’ll see how it shakes out. That’s how this always works. And, by the way, it’s done for Rs and Ds on both sides of the aisle.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Now, we should note both Representatives Miller and Mills deny the accusations against them, but isn’t it the case that the two parties hold their Members to a very different ethical standard?

LEADER JEFFRIES: I think, as Democrats, we’re going to continue to try to uphold an American standard of decency and fairness and ensuring, of course, that people get their due process in an administrative or legal or congressional process, while at the same time trying to uplift American values. And what Republicans are trying to do, of course, is just take a partisan approach to everything, and that’s just the reality. We’ve seen it over the last 18 months. And at the end of the day, Republicans are just all consumed with power, and not power to actually make life more affordable for the American people in the midst of a crisis where life is too expensive, they’re continuing to just lean into lifting up the wealthy, the well-off, and the well-connected.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Let’s switch gears to the House. As we mentioned, we’re closing in on 100 days until the election, and Democrats are honing their message and laying out their priorities. You’ve said the first bill of a new Democratic session would be focused on affordability. This week, Democrats in the House passed another resolution to halt U.S. military action in Iran, gaining four Republican votes in the process. You’ve called the Trump administration’s strategy with Iran, quote, ‘Operation Epic Failure,’ end of quote. Are voters responding to what you’re doing and saying, and are you confident your party can regain power in Congress this fall?

LEADER JEFFRIES: We’re definitely confident that we’re on the right side of the American people in terms of our commitment to drive down the high cost of living, to make sure that we actually deliver affordable healthcare for every single American and that we hold the crooks accountable in the midst of a level of corruption, the likes of which have never been seen in America’s 250-year history. Our agenda, of course, begins aggressively with addressing the affordability crisis. And we’re committed to lowering the cost of groceries, the cost of gas, the cost of housing, the cost of everyday goods, the things that are making life untenable for far too many Americans. We believe when you work hard and play by the rules in this country, you should be able to live a middle-class life, an affordable life, live the good life. That’s not the case right now. Far too many Americans are drowning in this failed Trump economy, and it’s time to move the country in a different direction.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Fox News polling out this week shows nearly 40% of voters want dramatic change right now, and Democrats are favored over Republicans on nearly every issue, including the economy and foreign policy. Republicans hold only slight edges on national security and crime, yet with their poll numbers plunging, Trump and Republicans have been focused on rigging the electorate in their favor. Tomorrow we’re going to be talking to your colleague Congressman Cleo Fields, who announced he will not be seeking re-election this week, after his majority-Black Louisiana district was eliminated in the wake of the Supreme Court Callais decision. You’ve been very clear that you view what happened to Representative Fields a form of voter suppression. A gut check question now: how deeply will this country be impacted in November by what Republicans and the courts have done to Black representation, and how are Democrats working to overcome it?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Congressman Cleo Fields will be deeply missed. We’re going to work closely over the next six or so months so he can finish out his term strong. He’s a tremendous champion for the people of Louisiana, and it’s a shame that his seat has been carved up as a result of the unprecedented attack on the Voting Rights Act by the Supreme Court, and then the Jim Crow-like tactics that have been unleashed in states like Louisiana as well as Tennessee and Alabama, signed off on by the United States Supreme Court, which is why we believe dramatic change is necessary in a whole host of areas—that’s dramatic campaign finance reform, dramatic electoral reform, including, of course, passage of the John Robert Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act so we can end the era of voter suppression in the United States of America once and for all. And certainly we need dramatic Supreme Court reform because this right-wing Supreme Court extremist majority is totally out of control and they need to be reigned in.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Now, President Trump and his allies continue to push for the so-called SAVE Act that includes many of the President’s vote supressing—suppression priorities and, like, voter ID. This week, House Republicans tucked elements of the SAVE Act into a budget reconciliation bill that passed along party lines, that Senate Majority Leader John Thune has said will not pass the Senate in its current form. Are you concerned Republicans could still find a way to push through parts of the SAVE Act before the midterms, and what are the Democrats doing to counter this?

LEADER JEFFRIES: We’re going to continue to stand strong against the voter suppression efforts of the Republican Party led by Donald Trump. Clearly, they have no agenda that they feel comfortable in selling to the American people because they’ve broken all their promises, including promising not to start forever wars in the Middle East, but to stop them. And then Donald Trump and Republicans turned around—they’ve gotten us involved in this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran. That, of course, has skyrocketed gas prices through the roof and are hurting everyday Americans day after day after day. And so, from our standpoint, we know that Republicans are going to try to rig the midterm elections. They’re doing it in real time. We’ve got to stop them from jamming this voter suppression bill down the throats of the American people. Democrats have been strong in the House and in the Senate in holding the line. We have to continue to do that. At the same period of time, we’re putting together the largest voter protection effort in the history of the country, working, of course, with Senate Democrats, House Democrats, the Democratic Governors Association, the Attorneys General Association on the Democratic side, the Democratic Secretaries of State, as well as civil society, which includes the faith community, civil rights groups, democracy protection groups, civil liberties groups, good government groups as well as organized labor. And together I’m confident we’re going to ensure that there’s a free and fair election in November.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Last question. I’m out of time, but I must ask you. Your Caucus is heading into an August recess with momentum toward the election but plenty of uncertainty. We don’t know what Trump and Republicans will do, how far they will go to try and undermine our democracy as they cling to power. We don’t know how tensions will play out between progressives and centrists inside the Democratic Party. So what’s your message to Members and to the candidates out there as we enter this critical stretch, the final 100 days?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Important for all of us to continue to keep the main thing the main thing. And that’s our commitment to fighting for an affordable America. Wherever one falls on the Democratic spectrum, we know that everyone is unified behind that fight. We want to lower the high cost of living for the American people. We want to make sure that there’s affordable healthcare for every single American. And we’re all committed to holding the crooks accountable and dealing with the rampant corruption that is undermining the Congress’ ability and our government’s ability to actually deliver for hardworking American taxpayers. Let’s keep the main thing the main thing. Let’s run through the finish line over the next 100 days or so. And then together, we can end this national nightmare, take back control of the Congress and continue our country’s march toward a more perfect union.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Well, thank you for being with us as we start the 100-day countdown to the election, Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries.

Full interview can be watched here.

###
title: LEADER JEFFRIES ON MS NOW: “IT’S TIME TO MOVE THE COUNTRY IN A DIFFERENT DIRECTION”

The Energy Department Continues to Deliver on President Trump’s Directive to Unleash American Nuclear Energy
July 25, 2026
THANKS TO PRESIDENT TRUMP, THE AMERICAN NUCLEAR RENAISSANCE HAS ARRIVED
- After decades of stagnation and regulatory paralysis, America's nuclear power industry is roaring back thanks to President Trump.
- On Friday, July 24, 2026, the Trump Administration celebrated achieving President Trump's ambitious goal of bringing three new advanced test reactors to criticality by July 4, 2026, as detailed in President Trump’s May 2025 executive order, “Reforming Nuclear Reactor Testing at the Department of Energy.” 
  - The Energy Department delivered and exceeded this milestone—achieving criticality of four advanced reactors by the July 4 deadline.
  - In total, President Trump has signed four executive orders related to unleashing commercial American nuclear energy: 
    - Deploying Advanced Nuclear Reactor Technologies for National Security – The White House
    - Ordering the Reform of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission – The White House
    - Reforming Nuclear Reactor Testing at the Department of Energy – The White House
    - Reinvigorating The Nuclear Industrial Base – The White House
- Under President Trump’s leadership, next-generation advanced reactors are moving toward deployment at a rapid pace, licensing has been streamlined, supply chains for nuclear fuel are being strengthened, and retired nuclear plants are being brought back online.
- Building out the next generation of American nuclear is an investment in our nation’s growing energy needs, and once built, these plants will deliver affordable, reliable electricity for generations to come.
THE ENERGY DEPARTMENT IS DELIVERING NEW ADVANCED NUCLEAR TECHNOLOGY
- In June 2025, the Energy Department launched the Reactor Pilot Program, to accomplish President Trump’s goal of accelerating the deployment of advanced reactors and achieving criticality of at least three reactors by America’s 250th birthday. 
  - In August 2025, Energy Department announced 11 initial selections for advanced reactor projects.
  - The 10 companies selected include: Aalo Atomics, Antares Nuclear, Atomic Alchemy, Deep Fission, Last Energy, Oklo, Natura Resources, Radiant Industries, Terrestrial Energy, and Valar Atomics.
  - Four of the Reactor Pilot Program projects would be hosted at the Idaho National Laboratory (INL) site, including Radiant (KDU), Antares (Mark-0), Aalo (Aalo-X), and Oklo (Aurora).
- On June 4, 2026, the Energy Department celebrated Antares Nuclear’s advanced reactor, Mark-0, successfully reaching criticality through a test demonstration at INL.
  - This achievement was the first time in over 40 years that a new privately developed non-light-water nuclear reactor reached criticality in America.
  - The zero-power fueled criticality demonstration confirmed the reactor would be able to operate safely and established a baseline for allowing subsequent reactors to produce electricity in 2027 and the following years.
- On June 18, 2026, the Energy Department announced Valar Atomics’ advanced test reactor, Ward 250, successfully reached criticality at the Utah San Rafael Energy Lab in Emery County, Utah.
- On June 30, 2026, Deployable Energy’s Unity completed a criticality demonstration, also hosted at INL—marking the third reactor to reach criticality ahead of the July 4 deadline.
- On July 4, 2026, Aalo Atomics’ test reactor, Aalo-X, completed a zero-power fueled criticality demonstration at INL, marking the fourth reactor to reach the Energy Department’s criticality milestone.
THE ENERGY DEPARTMENT IS SUPPORTING NEW NUCLEAR PROJECTS AND BRINGING REACTORS BACK ONLINE
- Thanks to the Office of Energy Dominance Financing (EDF), bolstered by the Working Families Tax Cut, the Energy Department is bringing previously shuttered nuclear power plants back online, and financing the development of new nuclear projects in the United States.
  - On June 23, 2026, the Energy Department announced financing for long-lead time supply chain items to accelerate the timeline for the deployment of 10 new large-scale commercial nuclear reactors.
  - The Energy Department is supporting the restart of previously shut-down nuclear power plants; including, Palisades 800 MW nuclear generating station in Michigan, and the Crane Restart project—an 835 MW nuclear plant in Pennsylvania. More restarts are expected to be announced in the future.
  - In March 2026, the Energy Department’s Office of Nuclear Energy (in collaboration with EDF) launched the Utility Power Reactor Incremental Scaling Effort (UPRISE) initiative to accelerate domestic nuclear energy production.
    - UPRISE aims to add 2.5 GW of nuclear capacity by 2027, and 5 GW by 2029—the equivalent of five new nuclear reactor years sooner than any other nuclear technology.
THE ENERGY DEPARTMENT IS UNLEASHING NUCLEAR INFRASTRUCTURE AND ADVANCING SUPPLY CHAINS FOR NUCLEAR POWER
- The Trump Administration and the Energy Department have taken sweeping, coordinated actions to rebuild U.S. nuclear infrastructure, restore America’s nuclear supply chain and support the entire nuclear lifecycle. 
  - April 9, 2025: The Energy Department made conditional commitments to provide high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) to five U.S. nuclear developers to meet their near-term fuel needs.
  - July 16, 2025: The Energy Department announced the start of the Fuel Line Pilot Program to accelerate the development of advanced nuclear reactors and strengthen domestic supply chains for nuclear fuel.
  - July 24, 2025: The Energy Department announced four site selections for AI data center and energy infrastructure development on federal lands—INL, Oak Ridge Reservation, Paducah Gaseous Diffusion Plant, and Savannah River Site.
  - August 26, 2025: The Energy Department made a second round of conditional commitments to provide HALEU to three U.S. companies to meet near-term fuel needs.
  - September 30, 2025: The Energy Department selected four companies for Advanced Nuclear Fuel Line Pilot Projects in order to strengthen domestic supply chains for nuclear fuel.
  - October 28, 2025: The U.S. Government established a strategic partnership with Cameco Corporation and Brookfield Asset Management to accelerate the development of Westinghouse’s nuclear reactor technologies in the United States and abroad.
  - December 2, 2025: The Energy Department awarded $800 million to TVA and Holtec to advance U.S. deployment of advanced light-water SMRs.
  - January 5, 2026: The Energy Department announced a $2.7 billion investment to strengthen domestic uranium enrichment, in support of President Trump’s commitment to expand U.S. capacity for low-enriched uranium and jumpstart new supply chains and innovations for high assay low enriched uranium.
  - January 28, 2026: The Energy Department released a Request for Information (RFI) for states to express interest in hosting Nuclear Lifestyle Innovation Campuses—a new effort to modernize the country’s nuclear fuel cycle.
  - February 5, 2026: The Energy Department awarded $19 million to five U.S. companies to research and develop recycling technologies for used nuclear fuel.
  - March 5, 2026: The Energy Department and the National Reactor Innovation Center (NRIC), announced the establishment of the Nuclear Energy Launch Pad—building on the Reactor Pilot Program and Fuel Line Pilot Program—to promote the development of advanced nuclear technologies by the private industry.
  - April 23, 2026: The Energy Department announced the Nuclear Fuel Cycle Consortium under the Defense Production Act, to secure the nation’s nuclear fuel supply chain and power the current nuclear reactor fleet.
  - May 14, 2026: The Energy Department announced the selection of eight companies to support the near-term deployment of advanced light-water small modular reactors (SMRs) in the United States.
To read more about the Trump administration’s efforts to unleash American nuclear energy, click here.
title: FACT SHEET: The Golden Era of American Nuclear Energy Has Arrived

HOUSTON, TX — Yesterday, Congressman Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) joined Congresswoman Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Congressman Adriano Espaillat (NY-13), Chair of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, Congressman Bennie G. Thompson (MS-02), Ranking Member of the House Committee on Homeland Security and 7 additional Members of Congress from across the country for a congressional hearing in Houston examining the fatal shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

Held at the Harris County Commissioners Court, right in Congressman Menefee’s district, the hearing brought Lorenzo's family, local officials, faith leaders, legal experts, and community advocates together to examine ICE's use of deadly force, the agency's lack of transparency, and the urgent need for accountability following Lorenzo's death.

Congressman Menefee questioned Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare about ICE agents' failure to wear body cameras during the fatal encounter, highlighting what both agreed is a striking departure from modern law enforcement practices.

Rep. Menefee: "Throughout your career, you've worked on thousands of cases involving local law enforcement, correct?"

District Attorney Sean Teare: "Yes."

Rep. Menefee: "It's standard practice in 2026 for law enforcement officers on the street to wear body cameras, correct?"

District Attorney Sean Teare: "Congressman, you and I have been in this very room talking about things like this. We have 86 law enforcement agencies that operate in Harris County alone. The only one that doesn't have body cameras is ICE."

Following the hearing, Congressman Menefee condemned the agency's lack of accountability.

"This is an agency that needs to be torn down to the studs and rebuilt into one that enforces immigration law while recognizing the dignity of every person it encounters," said Congressman Menefee. "We all know that won't happen under this Administration, and it won't happen under this Republican-controlled Congress."

Congressman Menefee also emphasized that meaningful oversight will require a change in congressional leadership, stating that if Democrats regain control of the U.S. House of Representatives after the November midterm elections, one of their first priorities will be conducting a full congressional investigation into the death of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo and other deaths involving ICE agents since President Donald Trump returned to office in 2025.

Since Lorenzo's death, Congressman Menefee has repeatedly called for the immediate release of all unedited evidence, including body camera and dash camera footage, demanded an independent investigation into the shooting, and pushed for transparency and accountability for Lorenzo's family and the Houston community.
title: Rep. Menefee Joins Congressional Leaders in Houston to Demand Answers in the Killing of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo

Hernández propone reforma al financiamiento de campañas para combatir "la corrupción de la claque”
CAYEY, Puerto Rico — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández, marcó hoy el 74.º aniversario del Estado Libre Asociado con un mensaje contundente contra lo que denominó "la corrupción de la claque": una red de funcionarios de distintos partidos que, según Hernández, antepone intereses propios al servicio público y pone en riesgo miles de millones en fondos federales de reconstrucción. "La claque son los que se compran y se venden, los que confunden servir con servirse", afirmó, citando casos recientes de nombramientos y contratos gubernamentales cuestionados.
Entre ellos, el escándalo en el Departamento de Desarrollo Económico y Comercio que llevó al senador federal Mike Lee a cuestionar directamente a la gobernadora sobre el manejo de fondos de reconstrucción. El riesgo, dijo Hernández, no es hipotético: la semana pasada el Departamento de Vivienda federal congeló más de $1,000 millones destinados a las Islas Vírgenes tras hallazgos de corrupción. "No queremos que eso le pase a Puerto Rico", advirtió.
Para atajar ese riesgo, Hernández identificó el financiamiento de campañas como una de las causas principales de la corrupción pública en Puerto Rico y presentó cuatro reformas para controlar el inversionismo político:
- Limitar más o prohibir los donativos en efectivo, para dificultar el lavado de dinero.
- Limitar más o prohibir los donativos anónimos, luego de que candidatos a la gobernación y partidos recibieran más de $1 millón de fuentes anónimas en las pasadas elecciones.
- Limitar más o prohibir las donaciones de contratistas del Gobierno, para reducir el inversionismo político.
- Requerir que las campañas divulguen dónde trabaja cada donante de cierta cantidad, y que el Contralor Electoral publique esa información.
La urgencia, explicó, está en lo laxo de las reglas actuales frente a las federales: un contratista federal no puede donar a candidatos federales, pero uno estatal en Puerto Rico puede donar hasta $3,300 a un candidato estatal. Además, puede donar hasta $3,300 en efectivo, contrario al límite de $100 en efectivo a nivel federal. A eso se suma el abuso de la regla que permite $50 en donativos anónimos, que fueron más de $1 millón de dólares entre todos los candidatos y partidos en 2024.
Hernández ilustró el riesgo de ese vacío: "Un contratista saca $100,000 en efectivo. Ese dinero se disfraza como donativos anónimos de $50 en un radiomaratón, o se reparte entre decenas de empleados públicos para que compren, a su nombre, boletos de $2,500 a un evento político. Violaron la ley, pero no hay manera efectiva de detectarlo: nadie tiene cómo saber de dónde salió el dinero, ni cuestionar cómo un empleado público que vive cheque a cheque tiene $2,500 en efectivo para donar a un político. El candidato gana — y el contratista recupera su inversión con un contrato de gobierno muy superior a los $100,000 originales.”
Hernández reconoció que no le sorprendería que personas de otros partidos ya hayan propuesto implantar restricciones similares en Puerto Rico. “Si es así, me uno a ellos. Las ideas no son de un líder, partido, o alianza … las ideas simplemente son buenas o malas. Y debemos estar con las ideas buenas, siempre.”
El mensaje llega una semana después de que Hernández señalara públicamente, en Barranquitas, a funcionarios de varios partidos vinculados a nombramientos y contratos cuestionados — señalamientos que, según dijo, ya provocaron la salida de algunos de sus puestos.
Hernández cerró invocando la constitución de 1952 y las palabras de Luis Muñoz Marín sobre la responsabilidad de sembrar bien para las generaciones futuras, y concluyó con un llamado que repitió tres veces: "El pueblo contra la claque”.
Puede ver una conferencia de prensa después del evento AQUÍ.
###
title: Hernández propone reforma al financiamiento de campañas para combatir "la corrupción de la claque”

The Trump Administration is Accelerating Scientific Discovery, Securing American Technological Leadership, and Building the Next Generation of American Scientists
October 9, 2026
- On Thursday, October 8, 2026, the Energy Department announced new initiatives and investments at the Science: A New Golden Age Summit to strengthen American scientific leadership, accelerate innovation, and secure U.S. technological dominance for generations to come.
  - These announcements deliver on key elements of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy’s (OSTP) July 2026 Golden Age report and advance the Energy Department’s Genesis Mission.
“We’re in the midst of a profound transformation in how science is conducted and breakthroughs are achieved. The convergence of Super Intelligence, high-performance computing, quantum, advanced scientific instruments, and automation empowers us to dramatically accelerate the productivity and impact of American science. Through the Genesis Mission and the investments announced today, we are building the capabilities, strategic partnerships, and scientific workforce required for the U.S. to lead this new era of discovery.” 
–Under Secretary for Science Dr. Darío Gil  
REVITALIZING THE AMERICAN SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY ENTERPRISE
- The Energy Department is accelerating scientific discovery and strengthening American innovation through new research investments and initiatives, including:
  - Investing $96 million in 67 awards through the Energy Department’s Office of Science Early Career Research Program to support the next generation of American scientific leaders. 
    - The awards will support 48 scientists at universities and 19 scientists at Energy Department National Laboratories.
  - Launching a new metascience initiative to advance the Genesis Mission’s goal of doubling the scientific productivity and impact of American research and development.
  - Establishing a new “Golden Ticket” pilot program through the Energy Department’s Office of Science to provide reviewers with greater flexibility to support bold, high-risk research ideas that challenge conventional thinking and could unlock entirely new fields of scientific discovery. 
SECURING AMERICAN TECHNOLOGICAL DOMINANCE
- The Energy Department is advancing cutting-edge technologies in robotics, autonomous science, and quantum computing to strengthen American technological leadership through the following initiatives:
  - Investing $30 million over three years in four National Laboratory-led robotics and autonomous-science testbeds to accelerate the development and deployment of advanced scientific capabilities. 
    - The testbeds will integrate embodied SI, robotics, laboratory automation, digital twins, and advanced computing to develop reusable capabilities across the Energy Department’s National Laboratories and User Facilities.
  - Identifying eight Quantum Genesis Priority Applications to guide the Quantum Genesis Mission’s efforts to develop fault-tolerant, scientifically relevant quantum computers. 
    - These priority applications will focus efforts on key scientific utility problems and help advance American leadership in quantum computing.
UNLEASHING A GOLDEN AGE OF SUPERINTELLIGENCE-ENABLED SCIENCE
- The Energy Department is expanding Super Intelligence-enabled research, strengthening federal partnerships, and advancing scientific data capabilities through the Genesis Mission by:
  - Announcing 12 new Phase II and six Phase I Genesis Mission project awards to push the frontiers of SI-enabled scientific discovery. 
    - These awards bring the Genesis Mission’s first-year portfolio to 297 projects, advancing the use of SI to accelerate scientific breakthroughs. Learn more about the selected projects here.
  - Expanding the Genesis Mission Consortium through collaboration with the National Institutes of Health (NIH), National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), and Department of War (DOW).  
    - The expanded consortium will engage external partners and mobilize industry, academic, and nonprofit capabilities to advance Genesis Mission priorities.
  - Identifying 190 priority dataset repositories across 14 federal agencies aligned with the Genesis Mission’s National Science and Technology Challenges. 
    - These repositories will lay the initial foundation for government-wide data federation with the Genesis Mission Platform, expanding access to scientific data and strengthening SI-enabled research.
BUILDING THE NEXT GENERATION OF AMERICAN SCIENTIFIC LEADERS
- Under the Trump Administration, the Energy Department is expanding opportunities for young Americans to pursue careers in science and technology and preparing the next generation of scientific leaders through:
  - Launching a new Genesis Mission Graduate Fellowship to prepare American scientists to lead in SI-enabled research and discovery. 
    - The fellowship will support universities in developing and demonstrating innovative four-year PhD training programs that combine expertise in SI with a scientific discipline.
    - Selected students will participate in two research experiences: one at an Energy Department National Laboratory and another in private industry.
  - Establishing the Battelle-Genesis Mission High School Fellowship to introduce young Americans to cutting-edge scientific research and SI technologies.
    - The fellowship will train 20 students in its inaugural year, developing competencies in SI, science, and engineering research through experiences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL), Idaho National Laboratory (INL), or Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL).
title: FACT SHEET: The Energy Department is Ushering in a Golden Age of American Science
